claims.text: TypeSafe AI opened early access to Jev, their SystemOne model, in the week before this post.
GeoDeploy works across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud regions offering managed Kubernetes.
TypeSafe's Jev provides decision primitives: choice(), score(), and noul(), returning typed answers with calibrated confidence.
Jev's choice() picks one option from a closed list and returns the pick, a probability distribution across all options, and a confidence.
Jev's score() rates something against a rubric; GeoDeploy uses 10 levels.
Jev's noul() answers a yes/no question with a single probability.
GeoDeploy fetches current prices from the AWS Price List API, the Azure Retail Prices API, and the Google Cloud Billing Catalog.
GeoDeploy's module registry supports EKS, AKS, GKE; ECR, ACR, Artifact Registry; and DNS via Route 53, NS1, or Cloudflare.
GeoDeploy's Pulumi Automation API run does a preview then an update, with one stack per region, and won't run unless cloud credentials pass readiness checks.
Every GeoDeploy run writes plan.json and plan.md.
For each geo, GeoDeploy sends Jev a shortlist of up to 40 priced candidates.
The @typesafe-ai/sdk package exports choice, noul, and score.
The TypeSafeClient has a systemOne method taking state and questions and returning answers with fields like selection.choice, confidence, residencyOk.noul, coverage.score.
TypeSafe advises to 'describe situations, not degrees' for rubrics.
GeoDeploy ranking uses weight profiles: latency-optimized (default), balanced, residency-first, failure-domain.

Weight profile values: latency-optimized cost 0.13, coverage 0.48, maturity 0.17, sprawl 0.1, arch 0.12; balanced 0.25/0.25/0.2/0.12/0.18; residency-first 0.12/0.12/0.38/0.23/0.15; failure-domain 0.08/0.17/0.48/0.15/0.12.
AWS always means EKS and ECR in GeoDeploy's module selection.

GeoDeploy confidence thresholds: data residency 0.95 hard reject; new cluster region 0.90 flags top three; existing stack region 0.75 keep existing; ingress/autoscaling 0.85 registry default; node-pool tier 0.60 bin-packing; global floor 0.50 drops AI path.
GeoDeploy's engine.ts residency check hard-rejects below 0.95 in packages/decide/src/engine.ts.
Each AiPathAborted carries the full attempt (state, questions, answers).

On gate failure, API timeout/error, or unreachable upstream, GeoDeploy falls back to deterministic price comparison enforcing residency and constraint checks; `geodeploy explain` shows why each region won.

GeoDeploy's `geodeploy monitor` self-driving mode checks CPU utilization periodically and asks Jev one joint question; above 0.85 confidence resize is auto-applied, 0.70-0.85 suggested for human approval, below 0.70 falls back to a deterministic per-region rule.
CPU utilization alone is a poor autoscaling metric and is usually paired with other signals such as latency and error rates.
The Pulumi Automation API page exists at /automation/.
The GitHub repo pulumi/devx-geodeploy exists and is open source.
